author: zhaohuabing
body:
**Description**

This PR introduces MCP spec compatible scope based authorization for MCPRoutes.

According to the 2025-11-25 version of the MCP spec, the MCP Gateway should enforce scope-based authorization on behalf of the backend MCP server, and include the required scopes in the `WWW-Authenticate` header of the 403 response if authoriation fails.

https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization#runtime-insufficient-scope-errors

> When a client makes a request with an access token with insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with:
HTTP 403 Forbidden status code 
WWW-Authenticate header with the Bearer scheme and additional parameters:
error="insufficient_scope" - indicating the specific type of authorization failure
scope="required_scope1 required_scope2" - specifying the minimum scopes needed for the operation
resource_metadata - the URI of the Protected Resource Metadata document (for consistency with 401 responses)
error_description (optional) - human-readable description of the error

Example:

```yaml
spec:
  ...
  securityPolicy:
    oauth:
      ...
    authorization:
      rules:
        - source:
            jwt:
              scopes:
                - echo
          target:
            tools:
              - backend: mcp-backend-authorization
                toolName: echo
                when: args.text.matches("^Hello, .*!$")
        - source:
            jwt:
              scopes:
                - sum
          target:
            tools:
              - backend: mcp-backend-authorization
                toolName: sum
```

Reference: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization#scope-challenge-handling

Implements #1459

**Created 5 issue form templates** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`):
- **add-new-activity.yml** - Add extracurricular activities with structured schedule/capacity fields
- **modify-activity.yml** - Update existing activity details with change type selection
- **bug-report.yml** - Report issues with severity classification and reproduction steps
- **ui-enhancement.yml** - Request styling changes with current/desired state comparison
- **feature-request.yml** - Propose new functionality with user stories and priority

**Each template provides**:
- Required field validation (dropdowns, checkboxes, inputs)
- Pre-filled acceptance criteria checklists
- "Implementation Notes for Copilot" sections with:
  - Target file paths (`src/backend/database.py`, `src/static/*.css`)
  - Code structure examples
  - Format constraints (24-hour time, exact day names)

**Example template section**:
```yaml
- type: markdown
  attributes:
    value: |
      ### Implementation Notes for Copilot

         - Activity name as key
         - schedule_details: {days: ["Monday"], start_time: "15:30", end_time: "17:00"}
         - max_participants as integer

```

body:
Implements traffic signal camera analysis system that counts pedestrians, 2-wheelers, 4-wheelers, detects violations, and adjusts signal timing based on traffic density.

## Core Implementation

**Traffic Analysis Page** (`src/app/traffic-monitoring/page.tsx`)
- Real-time detection dashboard with 3-second update intervals
- Vehicle/pedestrian counters with live statistics
- Violation tracking panel with severity categorization (low/medium/high)
- Signal timing control with AI recommendations (45s-90s based on density)
- Analytics tabs: Summary, Density Analysis, Configuration

**AI Flow Integration** (`src/ai/flows/analyze-traffic.ts`)
- Genkit-based traffic analysis flow
- Returns structured data: vehicle counts, pedestrian count, violations array, density classification
- Designed for easy swap to real computer vision models (YOLO, TensorFlow Object Detection)

**Server Actions** (`src/app/traffic-monitoring/actions.ts`)
- Server-side wrapper for AI flow invocation
- Error handling and data validation layer

## Architecture Decisions

Simulation layer allows immediate testing without camera infrastructure. Production integration requires:
```typescript
// Replace simulated analysis with real CV model
const analysis = await analyzeTrafficFromVideoFrame(frameBuffer, {
  model: 'yolov8',
  classes: ['person', 'motorcycle', 'car', 'truck'],
  violationDetectors: ['red_light', 'wrong_lane', 'no_helmet']
});
```

Signal timing algorithm:
- <10 vehicles: 45s
- 10-30 vehicles: 60s  
- 30-50 vehicles: 75s
- \>50 vehicles: 90s

body:
_Posting to get some conversation going around openness to using `fgetpwent_r` on the platforms that provide it (i.e., Linux)._

Per docs, it's *actually* reentrant and could be used to implement a non-unsafe version of group and user enumeration on the platforms that support it. That somewhat begs the question of whether it's feasible (and/or a good idea) to provide functions that are only unsafe on some platforms. It would be great to get your feedback on whether you'd consider something in this direction.

_(Aside: [this macOS man page](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/getpwent.3.html) indicates that `getpwent` *is* thread-safe on *that* platform because they happen to place its internal buffer in a thread-specific structure. Would need to more properly validate that, though.)_

body:
Created comprehensive bilingual documentation explaining ChemCPA's architecture and loss function design in response to request: "帮我查看ChemCPA的整体框架，以及其是怎么设计Loss的"

## Documentation Structure

- **`docs/FRAMEWORK_SUMMARY.md`** (315 lines, bilingual)
  - Quick reference: architecture overview, loss components, key hyperparameters
  - Code examples for model creation and prediction
  
- **`docs/FRAMEWORK_AND_LOSS_DESIGN.md`** (749 lines, Chinese)
  - Detailed architecture breakdown: Encoder, Decoder, Drug Embeddings, Dosers, Adversaries
  - Mathematical formulations for all loss components
  - Training strategies: alternating optimization, gradient reversal, learning rate scheduling
  - Evaluation metrics: R², Log-Fold Change, Disentanglement scores

- **`docs/LOSS_VISUALIZATION.md`** (498 lines, bilingual)
  - ASCII flow diagrams showing training process
  - Visual breakdown of loss computation and alternating optimization
  - Debugging guide with common issues and solutions

- **`docs/README.md`** (296 lines)
  - Documentation index with recommended reading paths for different audiences
  - Quick navigation to relevant sections

## Key Technical Content Covered

**Loss Function Design:**
```python
# Adversary update (every 3 steps)
L_adversary = L_adv_drug + L_adv_cov + λ_penalty * L_penalty

# Autoencoder update (other steps)
L_autoencoder = L_recon - λ_drug * L_adv_drug - λ_cov * L_adv_cov
                         ↑
              Gradient reversal via negative sign
```

**Architecture Flow:**
```
genes → Encoder → latent_basal (drug-free via adversaries)
                      ↓
                  + drug_emb × doser(dose)
                  + covariate_emb
                      ↓
                  latent_treated → Decoder → (mean, variance)
```

**Core Design Principles:**
- Adversarial training with gradient reversal to disentangle drug/covariate from basal state
- Additive latent composition for generalization to novel drug-cell combinations
- Variance prediction for uncertainty quantification
- Three independent optimizers with alternating updates

Updated main `README.md` with links to new documentation.

body:
## Summary
Add simple size detection that keeps object shape constant while adjusting size between keyframes.

## Changes
- Added size metrics (width, height, scale) to object detection
- New `_calculate_scale_factor()` method computes size ratio between keyframes
- Modified `_render_object_frame()` to apply uniform scaling transformation
- Enhanced logging to show object sizes and scale changes

## How It Works
**Before**: Objects moved and changed color, but size stayed constant
**After**: Objects move, change color, AND scale smoothly

The transformation pipeline:
1. Center contour at origin
2. Apply interpolated scale: `scale(t) = (1-t) * 1.0 + t * scale_ratio`
3. Translate to interpolated position

**Result**: Objects grow/shrink smoothly while maintaining exact shape (no deformation)

## Testing
Verified with test showing blue ball scaling from 30px radius to 90px radius (3x growth):
- Size detection accurate (detected 2.97x vs expected 3.0x)
- Smooth interpolation across 9 frames
- Shape maintained perfectly (circle stays circular)
- No artifacts or distortion

author: copilot
body:
Tests failed under pytest due to data-dependent tensor indexing in `_find_best_split()` when `look_ahead=0`. The method used `torch.argmax()` results directly as tensor indices, which torch.compile() cannot handle in fullgraph mode.

## Changes

**Replaced direct tensor indexing with `torch.gather()` operations:**

```python
# Before: data-dependent indexing
best_feature = torch.argmax(max_decrease_per_feature)
best_split = best_split_per_feature[best_feature]  # ❌ Fails compilation
threshold_left = X[sorted_indices[best_split], best_feature]

# After: vectorized gather operations
best_feature_idx = torch.argmax(max_decrease_per_feature)
best_split_idx = torch.gather(best_split_per_feature, 0, best_feature_idx.unsqueeze(0)).squeeze(0)
# Use gather for feature columns and thresholds
X_feature_col = torch.gather(X, 1, best_feature_idx_expanded).squeeze(1)
threshold_values = torch.gather(X_feature_col.unsqueeze(0).expand(2, -1), 1, threshold_sample_indices.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
# Convert to Python int only at the end
best_feature = best_feature_idx.item()
```

**Key insight:** `torch.gather()` performs the same indexing operation but in a way that torch.compile() can trace and optimize. The `.item()` call happens outside the compiled computation graph.

Both `@torch.compile()` decorators on `fit()` and `predict()` remain intact. All 52 tests now pass.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Fix failing tests without removing @torch.compile() decorators from fit() and predict(). Refactor any remaining dynamic shapes, in-place updates or dynamic assignments which might cause problems for torch.compile. Use masks, torch.where and similar techniques like in most of regression_decision_tree.py.
> Also note that running fit() and predict() outside of pytest, from a regular python script, doesn't seem trigger these errors. It could be the issue is with the tests.


</details>



<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT TIPS -->

body:
This pull request refactors the settings persistence mechanism in the `SettingsService` class to use Java's `Preferences` API instead of file-based storage. This change streamlines how user settings are saved and loaded, improving reliability and simplifying the code. The most important changes are grouped below.

Settings persistence refactor:

* Replaced file-based settings storage (using `Properties` and file I/O) with the Java `Preferences` API, eliminating the need for manual file handling and reducing potential errors. (`SettingsService.java` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5152a4a5dd82742d2242aa4533628236af53ebf7a20ace98643190258d086751L3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5152a4a5dd82742d2242aa4533628236af53ebf7a20ace98643190258d086751L29-R31)
* Updated the `loadSettings` and `saveSettings` methods to use `Preferences` methods for reading and writing user settings, and removed exception handling related to file operations. (`SettingsService.java` [tetris-client/src/main/java/seoultech/se/client/service/SettingsService.javaL62-R82](diffhunk://#diff-5152a4a5dd82742d2242aa4533628236af53ebf7a20ace98643190258d086751L62-R82))

Default settings handling:

* Changed `restoreDefaults` to always call `saveSettings`, ensuring that default settings are persisted immediately. author: betooxx-dev
body:
# PULL REQUEST - FEAT FPC ANALYZER AND GENERAL IMPROVES

## Descripción

Este PR introduce una **expansión masiva** de las capacidades de análisis estático, centrada en la calidad del código de Machine Learning. Añade dos analizadores completamente nuevos: **`FPCAnalyzer`** (Cohesión Funcional del Pipeline) y **`FileStructureAnalyzer`** (calidad arquitectónica).

Además, refactoriza el motor de análisis central para usar un **Contexto Global (`AnalysisContext`)** que cachea ASTs y código fuente, mejorando drástantemente el rendimiento. Finalmente, introduce un **sistema de documentación de métricas** para que cada resultado de la API explique qué significa.

## Problema o contexto

El motor de análisis existente se limitaba a métricas genéricas (Pylint, Radon) que no evaluaban la calidad específica del código de un pipeline de ML.

1.  **Falta de Cohesión:** No podíamos detectar si un fichero (`.py`) mezclaba incorrectamente múltiples etapas del pipeline (ej. `data_collection` y `model_training`), lo cual es un anti-patrón.
2.  **Falta de Estructura:** No podíamos identificar anti-patrones arquitectónicos, como mezclar código ejecutable ("loose code") con definiciones de clases o funciones (`mixed_script`).
3.  **Ineficiencia:** Cada analizador leía y "parseaba" los mismos ficheros de forma redundante, causando problemas de rendimiento.
4.  **Resultados Crípticos:** La API devolvía un `score` sin explicar cómo se calculaba o cómo interpretarlo.

## Cambios realizados

Este PR es casi en su totalidad la adición de nuevas funcionalidades (2,128 líneas añadidas):

### 1\. Nuevo Analizador: `FPCAnalyzer` (Functional Pipeline Cohesion)

Se añade un analizador de cohesión funcional (`src/analyzers/fpc/fpc_analyzer.py`) que evalúa si los ficheros se mantienen enfocados en una única etapa o fase del pipeline de ML.

  * **Refactorización:** El antiguo `fpc_analyzer.py` fue eliminado y reemplazado por un módulo completo (`src/analyzers/fpc/`).
  * **Sub-componentes Nuevos:**
      * **`MLContentAnalyzer`**: Un nuevo analizador (`src/analyzers/ml_content/`) que detecta contenido no relacionado con ML (ej. `Flask`, `Tkinter`, `Streamlit`) para que FPC pueda excluir estos ficheros de su puntuación.
      * **`NLOCCalculator`**: Una nueva utilidad (`src/analyzers/fpc/nloc_calculator.py`) para calcular "Líneas de Código No Comentadas" (NLOC) y marcar ficheros demasiado pequeños.
      * **`FPCEvaluator`**: Un nuevo motor de reglas (`src/analyzers/fpc/fpc_evaluator.py`) que usa `fpc_rules.json` para generar diagnósticos y recomendaciones detalladas.

<!-- end list -->

```python
// src/analyzers/fpc/fpc_analyzer.py (NUEVO)
class FPCAnalyzer(BaseAnalyzer):
    def __init__(self, session_id: str, local_path: str, context=None):
        super().__init__(session_id, local_path, context)
        # ...
        self.ml_content_analyzer = MLContentAnalyzer(...)
        self.nloc_calculator = NLOCCalculator(...)
        # ...
        self.evaluator = FPCEvaluator()

    def analyze(self) -> AnalysisResult:
        # Usa el 'context' global para obtener los ficheros
        python_files = self.context.get_python_files()
        messages_list = []
        
        for py_file in python_files:
            # ... (calcula cohesión, ml_content, nloc)
            file_result = self._analyze_file(tree, source, py_file)
            
            # Genera diagnóstico (ej: "Este módulo mezcla 2 fases")
            evaluation = self.evaluator.evaluate_file(py_file, file_result)
            if evaluation:
                messages_list.append(evaluation)
        
        return self._create_result(
            score=round(score, 2),
            messages=messages_list,  # Nuevo formato de mensajes
            ...
        )
```

-----

### 2\. Nuevo Analizador: `FileStructureAnalyzer`

Se añade un analizador de arquitectura (`src/analyzers/file_structure_analyzer.py`) que detecta patrones de diseño y anti-patrones en cada fichero.

  * Clasifica los ficheros en 5 tipos:
      * `classes_only` (Buen OOP)
      * `functions_only` (Buen estilo funcional)
      * `script_only` (Código suelto, "loose code")
      * `mixed` (Anti-patrón: mezcla clases y funciones)
      * `mixed_script` (Anti-patrón Crítico: mezcla código suelto con clases/funciones)

<!-- end list -->

```python
// src/analyzers/file_structure_analyzer.py (NUEVO)
class FileStructureAnalyzer(BaseAnalyzer):
    
    def _classify_file_pattern(self, tree: ast.Module) -> str:
        # ... (detecta has_classes, has_top_level_functions, has_loose_code)

        has_structured = has_classes or has_top_level_functions

        if has_loose_code and has_structured:
            # Anti-patrón crítico
            return 'mixed_script'
        elif has_classes and has_top_level_functions:
            # Anti-patrón
            return 'mixed'
        elif has_classes and not has_top_level_functions and not has_loose_code:
            return 'classes_only'
        # ...
```

-----

### 3\. Refactorización del Núcleo: `AnalysisContext` y `BaseEvaluator`

Se refactoriza el motor de análisis para mejorar la eficiencia y extensibilidad.

  * **`AnalysisContext` (Nuevo)**: Se añade un contexto global (`src/core/analysis_context.py`) que se comparte entre todos los analizadores.
      * Gestiona la **lógica de descubrimiento de ficheros** (modo `all_files` vs. modo `ml_only`).
      * **Almacena en caché los AST y el código fuente** de los ficheros, evitando que cada analizador lea del disco y parsee el código repetidamente.
  * **`BaseEvaluator` (Nuevo)**: Se añade una clase base (`src/analyzers/base_evaluator.py`) para crear evaluadores basados en reglas (usado por `FPCEvaluator`).
  * **Endpoint `/analyze` (Refactorizado)**: El endpoint (`src/api/routes.py`) ahora crea el `AnalysisContext` y lo inyecta en cada analizador a través de la `AnalyzerFactory`.

<!-- end list -->

```python
// src/api/routes.py (MODIFICADO)
def analyze_session(session_id: str):
    # ...
    # Flag para analizar todos los ficheros o solo los de ML
    all_files = data.get('all_files', False) 

    from core.analysis_context import AnalysisContext
    shared_context = AnalysisContext(
        session_id, 
        session.local_path,
        pipeline_metadata=pipeline_metadata,
        all_files=all_files
    )
    
    for analyzer_type in analysis_request.analyzers:
        # ...
        # Inyecta el contexto compartido en cada analizador
        analyzer = AnalyzerFactory.create_analyzer(
            analyzer_type, session_id, session.local_path, shared_context
        )
        result = analyzer.analyze()
        results[analyzer_type] = result
```

-----

### 4\. Nuevo Sistema de Documentación de Métricas

Se añade un sistema de registro de métricas (`src/core/metrics/`) para que cada respuesta de la API se auto-documente.

  * `AnalysisResult` ahora incluye un campo `metric_metadata`.
  * La respuesta de la API (`to_dict()`) ahora serializa un nuevo campo `documentation` que explica la métrica, su fórmula y cómo interpretarla.

<!-- end list -->

```python
// src/core/models/analysis_result.py (MODIFICADO)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AnalysisResult:
    # ...
    metric_metadata: 'MetricMetadata'
    # ...
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "analyzer_id": self.analyzer_id,
            "score": self.score,
            "messages": self._serialize_value(self.messages),
            # ...
            "documentation": self.metric_metadata.to_dict() # <-- CAMPO NUEVO
        }

// src/core/metrics/registry.py (NUEVO)

    "radon_cc": MetricMetadata(
        metric_id="radon_cc",
        name="Cyclomatic Complexity",
        description=(...),
        formula="CC = E - N + 2P (...)",
        ...
    ),

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for OpenMemory, a self-hosted, open-source memory system for AI agents that was recently added to ADK. The PR includes:

1. **Complete documentation** for OpenMemory in `docs/sessions/memory.md`, including installation, configuration, setup instructions, and usage examples
2. **CLI usage examples** showing how to use OpenMemory with `--memory_service_uri` flag
3. **Comparison table updates** adding OpenMemory as a third memory service option alongside InMemoryMemoryService and VertexAiMemoryBankService

This documentation makes OpenMemory fully accessible to users, providing clear guidance on installation, setup, configuration, and usage patterns.

## Related PRs

- **Implementation PR**: https://github.com/google/adk-python/pull/3386
  - This PR implements the OpenMemory feature documented here
  - Includes core OpenMemoryService implementation, CLI URI support, and sample agent
  - The CLI examples in this documentation match the implementation in that PR

## Link to Issue or Description of Change

**2. No existing issue - documentation for existing OpenMemory feature**

**Problem:**

Following the OpenMemory implementation in `adk-python`, users needed:
- Complete documentation covering installation, setup, configuration, and usage patterns
- Comparison with other memory services to help users choose the right option
- Examples showing both CLI and programmatic usage
- Self-hosted setup instructions for Docker and Node.js deployments

**Solution:**

This PR provides:
- Full documentation section in `docs/sessions/memory.md` following the same pattern as Vertex AI Memory Bank
- Updated comparison table with OpenMemory as a third option
- CLI usage examples matching the implementation in `adk-python`
- Self-hosted setup instructions for Docker and Node.js deployments
- Advanced usage patterns and configuration options

## Changes

### Documentation Updates (`docs/sessions/memory.md`)

- **Updated comparison table**: Added `OpenMemoryService` as a third column with feature comparisons
  - Updated intro text from "two distinct" to "three distinct" implementations
  - Added rows for: Persistence, Primary Use Case, Memory Extraction, Search Capability, Setup Complexity, Dependencies, When to use it

- **New OpenMemory section** (after Vertex AI Memory Bank):
  - **Overview**: Description of OpenMemory as self-hosted, open-source memory system
  - **How It Works**: Explanation of two key operations (storing and retrieving memories)
  - **Key Features**: Multi-sector embeddings, graceful decay, server-side filtering, self-hosted, cost-effective
  - **Installation**: `pip install google-adk[openmemory]`
  - **Prerequisites**: Self-hosted backend setup and environment variables
  - **Configuration**: Two options:
    - **Option 1: CLI Usage** - Examples for `adk web` and `adk api_server` with URI formats
    - **Option 2: Python Code** - Manual instantiation examples
  - **Advanced Configuration**: `OpenMemoryServiceConfig` parameters documentation
  - **Self-Hosted Setup**: Docker and Node.js setup instructions with step-by-step guides
  - **Advanced Usage**: Multi-user isolation, app-level filtering, enriched content format
  - **Sample Agent**: Reference to sample agent in adk-python repository

- **Updated multi-memory service section**: Added OpenMemoryService to examples and updated code samples

## Technical Decisions

### Documentation Structure

The documentation follows the exact same structure as Vertex AI Memory Bank, ensuring consistency and making it easy for users to compare options. The side-by-side comparison table helps users quickly identify which memory service fits their needs.

### CLI Examples Alignment

All CLI examples in the documentation match the URI format implementation in `adk-python`:
- `openmemory://localhost:3000` format
- Query parameter support for API keys
- Full URL support

The examples are tested against the actual CLI implementation to ensure accuracy.

body:
Hello everyone,
I added the SSL_group_to_name entrypoint, as this is required by Debian 12 nginx.

The main changes are:

* Added a groups field to a SSLCtx, that contains all supported groups. This allows to implement the SSL_group_to_name entrypoint. The static C Strings are taken from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/eedb6df889fb69b9c4571be5616fa22e6b62dc7c/providers/common/capabilities.c#L154
* Added some more NIDs for Kyber groups

In future the groups could be used to implement the functions in https://docs.openssl.org/3.3/man3/SSL_CTX_set1_curves/.

I am happy to discuss the changes!

body:
## Summary
This PR integrates OpenAI's GPT-5-mini model with the assistant panel and adds DALL-E 3 student image generation capabilities.

### Key Features
- **Upgraded LLM Model**: GPT-4o-mini → GPT-5-mini for improved reasoning
- **Real-time Streaming**: Implemented Server-Sent Events for live response streaming
- **Student Image Generation**: DALL-E 3 integration with batch processing capability
- **Rate Limiting**: 10 chat requests/minute, 5 image requests/minute
- **Usage Tracking**: Comprehensive OpenAI API usage logging with cost estimation
- **PTM Component Preservation**: Parent-teacher meeting requests use existing component (no OpenAI text overlay)

### Technical Implementation

#### GPT-5-mini Configuration
- Model: `gpt-5-mini` (upgraded from `gpt-4o-mini`)
- Parameters:
  - `reasoning_effort: 'medium'` - Controls computational depth
  - `verbosity: 'medium'` - Controls output detail level
  - Streaming enabled for real-time responses

#### Database Schema
- **rate_limits** table: Tracks API requests per user for rate limiting
- **openai_usage** table: Comprehensive usage logging with cost tracking
- **Views**: Daily stats and usage summaries

#### File Structure
```
src/lib/openai/
├── client.ts           # OpenAI SDK configuration
└── rate-limit.ts       # Rate limiting and usage tracking

src/app/api/chat/
└── stream/route.ts     # Streaming chat endpoint with Edge runtime

src/app/actions/
└── openai-image-actions.ts  # DALL-E 3 image generation (single & batch)

src/components/student/
├── generate-photo-dialog.tsx      # Single student photo UI
└── batch-generate-dialog.tsx      # Batch generation UI

supabase/migrations/
└── 20251104160000_create_openai_infrastructure.sql  # DB schema
```

### Testing Notes
- ✅ Build passes with all TypeScript checks
- ✅ Rate limiting verified (10 chat/min, 5 images/min)
- ✅ Streaming responses functional
- ✅ PTM requests display component without OpenAI text
- ✅ Mock mode support for development
- ✅ Cost tracking operational

### Breaking Changes
None - backward compatible with existing functionality

### Migration Requirements
- Run Supabase migrations to create `rate_limits` and `openai_usage` tables
- Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable

author: copilot
body:
Entities become unavailable after initial pairing due to unreliable BLE connections and missing error handling for characteristic read failures. The integration uses direct `BleakClient.connect()` which triggers Home Assistant warnings and fails to recover from transient BLE errors.

## Changes

### Connection Management
- Replace `BleakClient` with `bleak-retry-connector`'s `establish_connection()` and `BleakClientWithServiceCache`
- Add disconnect callback for connection state monitoring
- Add `is_connected()` method for proper encapsulation

### Error Handling & Retry Logic
- Implement `_read_with_retry()` with exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s, capped at 10s)
- Handle `BleakCharacteristicNotFoundError` with service discovery checks before reads
- Use `ConfigEntryNotReady` for setup failures to enable automatic retry
- Check connection state before write operations

### Polling Improvements
- Detect disconnections and trigger automatic reconnection
- Separate error handling for characteristic, BLE, and generic errors
- Continue polling after failures instead of crashing

### Configuration
- Add constants for retry behavior: `MAX_READ_RETRIES`, `READ_RETRY_DELAY`, `MAX_RETRY_DELAY`, `RECONNECT_DELAY`, `SERVICE_DISCOVERY_DELAY`
- Update `manifest.json` to require `bleak-retry-connector>=3.1.0`

**Example retry logic:**
```python
async def _read_with_retry(self, characteristic: str, char_name: str) -> str:
    for attempt in range(MAX_READ_RETRIES):
        try:
            return (await self._read(characteristic)).decode('UTF-8')
        except BleakCharacteristicNotFoundError:
            delay = min(READ_RETRY_DELAY * (2 ** attempt), MAX_RETRY_DELAY)
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            if self.is_connected():
                _ = self._client.services  # Force service refresh
```

Also added `logo.svg`.

author: empiredan
body:
Fix https://github.com/apache/incubator-pegasus/issues/2281.

In `test_disable_backup_policy`, `continue_current_backup_unlocked()`
is invoked, which in turn calls `issue_new_backup_unlocked()` onto `_mp`
as the callback function where if `_policy.is_disable` is set to `true`, the
callback will recursively reschedule itself through the thread pool. After the
test has finished and `_mp` has been destructed, however, the background
thread may be still executing the callback, where accessing members inside
`_mp` will lead to a heap-use-after-free error. The solution is to stop all
running tasks on `_mp` before the unit test exits.

body:
## Summary

Fixed a critical bug where placements weren't being saved when editing GAM products because the save logic was nested inside an `if line_item_type:` check that never executed in automatic mode.

## Root Cause

The GAM product configuration save logic (lines 1147-1209 in `src/admin/blueprints/products.py`) was inside an `if line_item_type:` conditional. Since the edit form uses **automatic line item type selection** (based on pricing model), the form doesn't submit a `line_item_type` field. This caused the entire block to be skipped, preventing placements, ad units, targeting, and other GAM config from being saved.

## Changes

**File: `src/admin/blueprints/products.py`**
- Moved GAM config logic outside the `line_item_type` check
- Now checks `if adapter_type == "google_ad_manager"` instead
- Preserves existing implementation_config by starting with a copy
- Only regenerates default config when `line_item_type` is explicitly provided
- Allows placement/ad unit updates without full config regeneration

**File: `templates/add_product_gam.html`**
- Added defensive type checking for `targeted_placement_ids` (handles both string and array)
- Added console logging for troubleshooting placement population issues

## Testing

- All unit tests pass (861 passed, 7 skipped)
- All integration tests pass (32 passed)
- All integration_v2 tests pass (28 passed)
- Pre-commit hooks all pass (syntax, linting, type checking)

## Manual Testing Steps

1. Edit a GAM product with multiple placements
2. Change the placement selection (select different ones)
3. Save the form
4. Reload the edit page
5. Verify the new placements are displayed ✅

## Impact

- Placements now save correctly when editing GAM products
- Ad units now save correctly
- Custom targeting now saves correctly
- All GAM configuration updates are preserved
- Works in both automatic and explicit line item type modes

GoogleTest fails to compile on recent clang versions and is years out of date. Migrated to doctest, a modern single-header testing library with no external dependencies.

- **Replaced GoogleTest with doctest (v2.4.12)**
  - Removed `UnitTest/GoogleTest/` directory (~30K lines)
  - Added `UnitTest/doctest.h` and `doctest_main.cc`
  - Updated `UnitTestBase` to include doctest instead of gtest

- **Converted test macros**
  - `TEST(Suite, Name)` → `TEST_CASE("Suite - Name")`
  - `TEST_F(Fixture, Name)` → `TEST_CASE_FIXTURE(Fixture, "Fixture - Name")`
  - Added macro compatibility layer in `UnitTest.h` for `EXPECT_*`/`ASSERT_*` → `CHECK`/`REQUIRE`

- **Updated test fixtures**
  - Converted `SetUp()` → constructors, `TearDown()` → destructors
  - Removed `override` keywords and `::testing::Test` base class

author: adminguoyu
body:
This pull request implements full database integration for borrowing and returning books in the library system, replacing previous placeholders with actual SQL logic. It also makes a small schema change to the `Borrowings` table. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Database Integration for Borrowing and Returning Books:**

* Implemented SQL logic in `BorrowingManager` for borrowing a book by inserting a new record into the `Borrowings` table, including handling generated keys and error reporting.
* Implemented SQL logic in `BorrowingManager` for returning a book by updating the corresponding record, setting `return_date`, updating `status`, and clearing `file_path`. Added checks for valid `borrowing_id` and improved error handling.
* Fully implemented the `refresh()` method in `BorrowingList` to query the database for borrowings based on the last search, including support for filtering by book/user ID and status, and robust error handling for invalid input and SQL errors.

**Schema and Enum Adjustments:**

* Modified the `Borrowings` table schema to allow `file_path` to be nullable and not unique, enabling multiple borrowings without requiring a unique file path.
* Removed the unused `PUBLISHED_USER_ID` value from the `search_field` enum in `BorrowingList`.

**Dependency Imports:**

* Added necessary imports for SQL and utility classes in both `BorrowingList` and `BorrowingManager` to support the new database logic. body:
## Summary
Extends the `axual_application` resource to support additional application types (**Kafka Streams**, **Python**, **KSML**, and **Other**) and adds comprehensive testing coverage for all supported application types, including import validation.

## Motivation
The Axual platform supports multiple application types beyond the initially implemented **Java**, **Pega**, **SAP**, **DotNet**, and **Bridge**. This PR adds support for the missing application types and ensures they are properly validated and tested.

## Changes

### New Application Type Support
 - ✅ **Kafka Streams** - For Kafka Streams applications
 - ✅ **Python** - For Python-based applications
 - ✅ **KSML** - For KSML (Kafka Streams Markup Language) applications
 - ✅ **Other** - For any applications that is not matching the available types


  ### Resource Implementation
  - 📝 Updated `internal/provider/resource_application.go`:
    - Added new application types to the validator: `stringvalidator.OneOf()`
    - Updated schema documentation to reflect all supported types

  - 📝 Updated `docs/resources/application.md`:
    - Updated documentation to list all supported application types
    - Clarified which types are available for Custom vs Connector applications

### Testing
  - Added 11 new test configuration files for all application types:
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_java.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_kafka_streams.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_pega.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_sap.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_dotnet.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_bridge.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_python.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_ksml.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_other.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_sink.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_source.tf`
    - ✅ `axual_application_type_invalid.tf` (for negative testing)

  - 🔧 **Refactored resource naming** to follow Terraform best practices:
    - Changed from hyphenated (`tf-test-app`) to underscore format (`tf_test_app`)
    - Made all resource names unique and descriptive (e.g., `tf_test_app_type_java`, `tf_test_app_type_python`)
    - Eliminates naming conflicts and improves test clarity

  - 🧪 **Enhanced test suite** (`application_resource_test.go`):
    - Added new `TestApplicationResourceAllTypes` function
    - Tests creation and validation for all 10 application types
    - Added import state verification for all application types
    - Validates that invalid types are properly rejected

  - 📋 Updated existing test files:
    - `axual_application_initial.tf` - Updated resource naming
    - `axual_application_updated.tf` - Updated resource naming
    - `axual_application_invalid_uppercase.tf` - Updated resource naming


## Backward Compatibility

✅ **Fully backward compatible** - previously supported application types continue to work as before.

## Screenshots/Examples

Example usage in Terraform:

```hcl
# Kafka Streams Application
resource "axual_application" "tf_test_app_type_kafka_streams" {
  name             = "tf-test app type kafka streams"
  application_type = "Custom"
  short_name       = "tf_test_app_type_kafka_streams"
  application_id   = "tf.test.app.type.kafka.streams"
  owners           = data.axual_group.test_group.id
  type             = "Kafka Streams"
  visibility       = "Public"
  description      = "Test Application for Kafka Streams type"
}


# Python Application
resource "axual_application" "tf_test_app_type_python" {
  name             = "tf-test app type python"
  application_type = "Custom"
  short_name       = "tf_test_app_type_python"
  application_id   = "tf.test.app.type.python"
  owners           = data.axual_group.test_group.id
  type             = "Python"
  visibility       = "Public"
  description      = "Test Application for Python type"
}

```

author: salimomrani
body:
## 🎯 Problème résolu

À chaque redémarrage du serveur, l'IP change et le kubeconfig devient invalide. Il fallait manuellement régénérer et mettre à jour le secret `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA` en base64 dans GitHub Actions.

## ✅ Solution implémentée

**Utiliser kOps pour générer automatiquement le kubeconfig depuis S3** au lieu de le stocker manuellement.

## 📋 Changements

### 1. Workflow CI/CD (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- ➕ **Nouvelle étape**: Configuration des credentials AWS
- ➕ **Nouvelle étape**: Installation de kOps
- ➕ **Nouvelle étape**: Génération dynamique du kubeconfig depuis S3
- ➖ **Supprimée**: Décodage manuel du secret `KUBE_CONFIG_DATA`

### 2. Documentation (`.github/GITHUB_SECRETS_SETUP.md`)
- Guide complet pour configurer les secrets GitHub
- Instructions pour obtenir les credentials AWS
- Commandes pour vérifier kOps et la région AWS
- Permissions IAM requises

### 3. Script automatique (`.github/configure-secrets.sh`)
- Script Bash pour configurer automatiquement tous les secrets
- Récupère les credentials depuis les variables d'environnement
- Validation et affichage des secrets configurés

## 🔑 Nouveaux secrets GitHub requis

```bash
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID       # Credentials AWS
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   # Credentials AWS
AWS_REGION              # us-east-1
KOPS_STATE_STORE        # s3://kopsstate9569
KOPS_CLUSTER_NAME       # kubevpro.i-consulting.shop
```

## 🗑️ Secret obsolète

```bash
KUBE_CONFIG_DATA  # ❌ Plus nécessaire - peut être supprimé après test
```

## 🚀 Avantages

✅ **Pas de mise à jour manuelle** - kubeconfig régénéré automatiquement à chaque déploiement  
✅ **IP changeante = pas de problème** - kOps gère la configuration depuis S3  
✅ **Configuration centralisée** - Source unique de vérité dans S3  
✅ **Plus sécurisé** - Credentials AWS limités au lieu du kubeconfig complet  
✅ **Automatisation complète** - Script de configuration fourni  

## 📝 Plan de test

### Avant de merger :
1. **Configurer les secrets GitHub**:
   ```bash
   # Option automatique (recommandé)
   ./.github/configure-secrets.sh
   
   # Option manuelle
   gh secret set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -b "AKIA..."
   gh secret set AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY -b "..."
   gh secret set AWS_REGION -b "us-east-1"
   gh secret set KOPS_STATE_STORE -b "s3://kopsstate9569"
   gh secret set KOPS_CLUSTER_NAME -b "kubevpro.i-consulting.shop"
   ```

2. **Merger le PR**

3. **Vérifier le workflow CI/CD**:
   - Le workflow doit installer kOps
   - Générer le kubeconfig depuis S3
   - Se connecter au cluster avec succès
   - Déployer l'application

4. **Après confirmation** que ça fonctionne:
   ```bash
   gh secret remove KUBE_CONFIG_DATA
   ```

## 📚 Documentation

- **Setup guide**: `.github/GITHUB_SECRETS_SETUP.md`
- **Script auto**: `.github/configure-secrets.sh`

## 🔗 Références

- kOps state store: `s3://kopsstate9569`
- Cluster: `kubevpro.i-consulting.shop`
- AWS Account: `830495964247` (ansibleadmin)

author: jocaagura
body:
## [3.4.1] - 2025-11-04

### Fixed
- **Lints / Docs:**
    - Corrige advertencia _“Angle brackets will be interpreted as HTML”_ en DartDoc (`theme_usecases.dart`) escapando o envolviendo con código para tipos genéricos (`Either<ErrorItem, ThemeState>`).
- **UI (deprecations):**
    - Reemplazo de `toastStream` **deprecated** en `page_builder.dart`:
        - Ahora se usa `textStream` (solo texto) **o** `stream<ToastMessage>` según el caso, eliminando la dependencia de la API obsoleta.

### Changed
- **env (DI/testability)** — `hotfix(env): refactor Env for improved DI and testability`
    - `Env` pasa de diseño estático a **modelo basado en instancias**:
        - Convertido a `abstract class`; `isQa`, `isProd`, `mode` ahora son **getters de instancia**.
        - La variable de compilación `_mode` continúa siendo `static`, pero se **encapsula** detrás de la instancia.
    - **`DefaultEnv`**: implementación estándar por defecto.
    - **Testing:** se añade `modeTest` opcional para **forzar modo** en pruebas.
- **AppManager**
    - Ahora **recibe un `Env`** en el constructor (por defecto, `DefaultEnv`).
    - `appMode`, `isQa`, `isProd` delegan al `Env` **inyectado** (no más accesores estáticos).

### Docs
- Actualizada la documentación de `Env` y ejemplo práctico de uso con DI.
- Notas en `page_builder.dart` sobre el uso de `textStream`/`ToastMessage` en lugar de `toastStream`.

### Migration notes
- **Casi sin rompimientos**:
    - Si no pasas `Env`, **no debes cambiar nada** (usa `DefaultEnv`).
    - Para pruebas o entornos custom, inyecta tu instancia:
      ```dart
      final Env env = DefaultEnv(modeTest: AppMode.qa); // o tu implementación
      final AppManager am = AppManager(env: env);
      ```
    - Si tu UI usaba `toastStream` directamente, migra a:
        - `textStream` (cuando solo necesitas texto), o
        - un `Stream<ToastMessage>` si manejas tipos enriquecidos.

body:
Implements two new fire shader styles based on Studio Ghibli animation and modern cartoon aesthetics, expanding the tool from 2 to 4 professional-grade rendering modes suitable for anime and film production.

## Changes

### New Shaders

**Studio Ghibli 80s Shader** (`ghibli80s`)
- Layered ramp shading with 5 soft-transition color zones (ember red → golden yellow → warm white)
- Cel-shaded posterization (5 levels, 40% blend) for hand-painted aesthetic
- 3-octave FBM for traditional animation texture
- Soft outline rendering via edge darkening
- Full Navier-Stokes physics identical to realistic shader
- Performance: 7-12 FPS

**Modern Cartoon Shader** (`cartoon`)
- Flat shading with exactly 3 hard-edge color bands
- Bold black outlines (80% opacity)
- Simplified physics (no vorticity/pressure gradients)
- 1.15x saturation boost for vibrant appearance
- Performance: 15-25 FPS (fastest shader)

### Implementation

```javascript
// Ghibli: Layered ramp shading with smoothstep transitions
if (temp < 0.15) {
    color = vec3(0.35, 0.05, 0.15);  // Deep ember
} else if (temp < 0.3) {
    float t = smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, (temp - 0.15) / 0.15);
    color = mix(vec3(0.65, 0.08, 0.10), vec3(0.95, 0.20, 0.05), t);
}

// Cartoon: Hard-coded flat bands
float posterized = floor(flame * 3.0) / 3.0;
if (value < 0.3) color = vec3(0.8, 0.15, 0.0);
else if (value < 0.7) color = vec3(1.0, 0.55, 0.0);
else color = vec3(1.0, 0.95, 0.3);
```

### UI Updates

- 4 shader style buttons with cycle support via 'S' key
- Consistent parameter interface across all shaders (drag physics, buoyancy, vorticity, etc.)
- Updated labels: "Anime (Original)", "Ghibli 80s", "Modern Cartoon"

### Documentation

- **README.md**: Shader comparison matrix, usage recommendations, live demo link
- **SHADER_IMPLEMENTATION.md**: Technical reference with NPR techniques, color palettes, physics constants
- **INTEGRATION_SUMMARY.md**: Professional project overview

### Technical

- Standardized hash function constant (43758.5453123) across all shaders
- Zero security vulnerabilities (CodeQL verified)
- All shaders support identical parameter set for seamless switching

## Screenshots

## Stats

- 1,254 insertions, 40 deletions across 6 files
- 471 lines of shader code
- 3 comprehensive technical guides

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

body:
## Summary

This PR modernizes and cleans up the repository configuration, removing legacy cruft from the old setuptools/pip era and establishing consistent conventions for test artifacts, documentation, and tooling.

## Key Changes

### 1. Test Artifacts Consolidation
- **Centralized all test artifacts to `target/` directory** (Maven/Gradle convention)
- **Added `get_temp_dir()` function** to `chap_core/__init__.py` for single source of truth
- Replaced 7 hardcoded "target/" strings across 6 files with `get_temp_dir()` calls
- Updated core modules: `ExternalModelBase`, `NaivePredictor`, `vega_lite_dash`, `prediction_evaluator`
- Updated test fixtures and example scripts
- Simplified Makefile cleanup: single `rm -rf target/` instead of individual file deletions

### 2. Comprehensive .gitignore Cleanup
- **Removed 100+ lines of obsolete patterns** from old Python template
- Removed legacy build tools (setuptools/easy_install era): `.Python`, `eggs/`, `lib/`, `build/`, `.tox/`, etc.
- Removed unused testing patterns: `.hypothesis/`, `nosetests.xml`
- Removed obsolete framework patterns: Django, Flask, Scrapy, PyInstaller
- Removed Python 2 patterns: `*.pyo`, `*$py.class`
- Removed Jupyter notebook support (deleted `scripts/explorations/datatypes.ipynb`)
- Reorganized into 9 logical sections with clear headers
- **Result**: Clean, modern .gitignore (51 lines) reflecting actual project tooling (uv, hatchling, pytest, ruff)

### 3. Repository Configuration Fixes
- **Removed duplicate `httpx` dependency** from dev dependencies
- **Fixed pytest config**: Removed erroneous `tests/` from `norecursedirs`, added `target/`
- **Fixed runs/ pattern**: Changed `/runs` → `runs/` for consistency
- **Removed stray artifacts**: Deleted `model.pkl` and `predictions.csv` from project root
- **Updated make clean**: Added `site/` and `.cache` for complete cache cleanup

### 4. Documentation Restructuring
- **Renamed `docs_source/` → `docs/`** (standard convention for Sphinx source)
- **Unified output to `site/` directory** (consistent for local and CI builds)
- Updated all documentation build configs (Makefile, make.bat, GitHub Actions)
- Updated contributor documentation references
- **Benefits**: Clear separation (source in `docs/`, output in `site/`), less confusion for contributors

### 5. Configuration Consolidation
- **Deleted `setup.cfg`** (obsolete setuptools-era config file)
- All configuration now in single `pyproject.toml` file
- Removed obsolete entries: flake8 config, pytest config (already in pyproject.toml), bdist_wheel config

### 6. Tooling Cleanup
- **Removed all bumpversion/bump2version tooling**
  - Removed from pyproject.toml dependencies
  - Removed from GitHub Actions workflows
  - Deleted `.github/workflows/bumpversion.yml.disabled`
  - PyPI uploads remain available via manual workflow_dispatch trigger
  - Version management is now manual in `pyproject.toml`

## Benefits

- **Cleaner project structure** - Single `target/` directory for all build/test artifacts
- **Modern tooling** - Aligned with uv + hatchling + pytest + ruff stack
- **Consistent conventions** - Standard docs/ for source, site/ for output
- **Reduced complexity** - One config file (pyproject.toml), removed 4 obsolete tools
- **Less cruft** - Removed 150+ lines of obsolete configuration across multiple files
- **Better organization** - Logical grouping in .gitignore, clear build directories
- **Single source of truth** - `get_temp_dir()` function for temporary directory paths

## Test Results

All tests pass: **160 passed, 78 skipped, 6 xfailed, 1 xpassed**  
Documentation builds successfully to `site/html/`  
Lint passes with no errors

## Migration Notes

- Developers should run `make clean` to remove old artifacts
- Documentation now builds to `site/` instead of `docs/_build/` or `docs/`
- Version bumping is now manual in `pyproject.toml` (no automated tooling)
- Use `from chap_core import get_temp_dir` for temporary directory paths

K dispozici jsou nové routes:

- **/auth/signup** - Zahashuje heslo, vytvoří účet, do cookie přidá refresh token, v response vrátí access token
- **/auth/login** - Vyhledá účet podle e-mailu (později změníme třeba i na username), získá id účtu, do cookie přidá refresh token, v response vrátí access token
- **/auth/refresh** - Ověří existenci refresh tokenu, vygeneruje nové tokeny, do cookie přidá refresh token, v response vrátí access token

Auth bude později rozšiřován o OAuth přes sociální sítě, nebo rozšíření schématu uživatele

author: a11rew
body:
## Issue
`core` expects a `command` value to be passed in from the routing logic - the app router handler in this case, which is in the shape of an array containing the different command segments like ["document", "slug-for-cats"]. 

A truncated version of the array would get passed to `core` instead of the full command array causing `core` to always send the user to the 404 path for document requests, since it would always get a command array with one segment only.

## Changes
This PR fixes the core issue, adds disambiguation for the command used in the react-sdk vs the command passed to core so this is less likely to happen via a code change in the future. Unit tests included as well to prevent further regressions here.

author: garmashalex
body: Align PrimeField::NUM_BITS with the actual bit length of the scalar field modulus (order l) for Ed448, which is 446 bits (modulus starts with 0x3...). Previously set to 448, which incorrectly inflated CAPACITY and could break consumers relying on accurate NUM_BITS/CAPACITY. CAPACITY remains defined as NUM_BITS - 1 and now evaluates to 445 as intended.

author: timriley
body:
This was documented in the Hanami guides, but didn’t work in reality.

Here was the documented approach:

```ruby
# lib/foo_parser.rb
class FooParser
  def mime_types
    ['application/foo']
  end

  def parse(body)
    # manually parse body
  end
end

# config/app.rb
class App < Hanami::App
  config.middleware.use :body_parser, FooParser.new
end
```

With this change, we allow a single custom parser to be provided, but with these small changes to the setup:

1. It should inherit `Hanami::Middleware::BodyParser::Parser`
2. `mime_types` should be a class method
3. The class alone should be passed to the body parser, not the instance

So:

```ruby
# lib/foo_parser.rb
class FooParser < Hanami::Middleware::BodyParser::Parser
  def self.mime_types
    ['application/foo']
  end

  def parse(body)
    # manually parse body
  end
end

# config/app.rb
class App < Hanami::App
  config.middleware.use :body_parser, FooParser
end
```

Together with this change, everything will work.

We can update our docs for 2.3 to show this. We can also update our 2.0-2.2 docs to show this approach as working:

```ruby
config.middleware.use :body_parser, [FooParser]
```

How did we get into this situation? I think I'd chalk it up to Hanami Router’s body parser gear being a little bet old and not receiving enough attention during the upgrade. We could definitely streamline things further (e.g. I think inheriting from `Hanami::Middleware::BodyParser::Parser` shouldn't strictly be necessary), but this PR at least gets things into a better working state. I'd be happy to see those further improvements come in the future :)

Anyway, as I've mentioned elsewhere, I think the real future for body parsing (in full Hanami apps) is to move it to actions: https://github.com/hanami/hanami-controller/issues/484. We can still keep this capability in the router, of course, but reserve it for people who are choosing to use the router fully standalone.

Fixes https://github.com/hanami/hanami/issues/1377.

@krzykamil — since you raised https://github.com/hanami/hanami/issues/1377 (thank you!), how does this feel to you?

body: **Export Cloud Build Logs and PR Commenting Workflow** This pull request introduces a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically detects failed Cloud Build checks, fetches their logs, uploads them as artifacts, and posts a PR comment with direct links to the logs for easy debugging. **What this PR adds** - Workflow detects failed Cloud Build checks on pull requests. - Fetches error logs for each failed build. - Uploads logs as downloadable artifacts attached to the workflow run. - Adds PR comment with downloadable artifact links. **PR Comment Behavior** Posting: - If tests fail for the first time on a pull request, the workflow will post a new comment containing direct links to the error log artifacts. Updating: - If tests fail again on a subsequent commit, the workflow checks for an existing comment. If found, it updates the comment with the latest log links, ensuring the information is current. - Deleting: - If all tests pass on a new commit, the workflow checks for an existing error log comment. If one exists, it deletes the comment to indicate that all checks now pass. **Where are the logs saved?** - Logs are saved as workflow run artifacts in GitHub Actions. - They are not stored in any external bucket (e.g., Google Cloud Storage). - Artifacts are accessible via the GitHub Actions UI and direct links in the PR comment. **Retention Policy** - Artifacts are retained for 15 days (as set in the workflow: retention-days: 15). - After 15 days, logs are automatically deleted by GitHub. - If longer retention is needed, download the logs before expiration. **Requirements for Upstream Repository** - Google Cloud Service Account - Add a repository secret named GCLOUD_SERVICE_KEY containing a Google Cloud service account key (JSON). - The service account must have the following roles: - roles/cloudbuild.builds.viewer (Cloud Build Viewer) - roles/logging.viewer (Logs Viewer) **How it works** - On failed Cloud Build checks, the workflow fetches logs and uploads them as artifacts. - A PR comment is posted or updated with direct links to the log artifacts for easy access. - If all checks pass, any previous log comment is deleted. **Debugging Log Fetch Failures for External Contributors** - Download the artifact from the PR comment link for the failed build. - Open the artifact and review its contents: - If logs were fetched, you’ll see the error output from the build. - If fetching failed, you’ll see an error message (e.g., permission denied, build not found) and a build details URL. **Tested in fork:** This workflow has been tested in my fork with my own service account credentials and is working as intended. **Reference Image**

body:
## Context

https://github.com/getlago/lago/commit/2747b04ea90c8b87c0413f07bda117547176a52f introduced a PG init script which was meant to create the database. Due to a typo in the file path, it was never used by PG.

Later on, https://github.com/getlago/lago/commit/52ab3b351bac47980969978b98edea1aa637c587 introduced two `bootstrap.sh` which are not used.

## Description

This removes the `bootstrap.sh` and fixes the PG init script.

Note that the PG Docker image automatically creates a user and database based on the `POSTGRES_USER` and `POSTGRES_DB` variables. Since `POSTGRES_USER` is not defined, it will use `POSTGRES_USER` for both user and password:

```
/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh: running /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/create-multiple-postgresql-databases.sh
Multiple database creation requested: lago,lago_test
Creating user and database 'lago'
Database lago already exists.
Granted privileges on database lago to user lago.
Creating user and database 'lago_test'
Database lago_test created.
Granted privileges on database lago_test to user lago.
Multiple databases created
```

author: vivmadigan
body:
This pull request introduces comprehensive improvements to the project's code coverage workflow, documentation, and reporting accuracy. The main focus is on ensuring that only relevant code is included in coverage metrics, providing clear guidance for running and interpreting coverage reports, and establishing robust CI/CD enforcement. These changes will help the team accurately track and improve test coverage, avoid misleading statistics caused by generated code, and streamline both local and CI-based coverage processes.

**Key changes include:**

### 1. Accurate Coverage Reporting & Exclusions

- Added and documented explicit exclusion filters for EF Core migrations, DTOs, entities, designer files, and other auto-generated code across coverage scripts (`coverage.ps1`, `coverage.sh`) and configuration files. This prevents non-testable code from skewing coverage statistics and ensures reports reflect actual application code coverage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fbd04b0cf60f5c013a1db895e84ab002ab8bda5874a4811f53504e3fd370ca02R1-R162) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bbbdc3a245e2ea49b497c1160140b3f87bf28f2c56d160b8fe0bdefcb26e83b7R1-R104) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c7caa57d888b77c1137643d873343d442bed26f88be2726609b63ba08e0908afR1-R53)
- Updated `ReportGenerator` usage to include class filters, ensuring migrations and other excluded files are omitted from HTML and summary reports. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bbbdc3a245e2ea49b497c1160140b3f87bf28f2c56d160b8fe0bdefcb26e83b7R1-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c7caa57d888b77c1137643d873343d442bed26f88be2726609b63ba08e0908afR1-R53)

### 2. Documentation & Quick Reference

- Added detailed guides (`COVERAGE.md`, `COVERAGE_QUICKSTART.md`, `COVERAGE_QUICK_REF.md`, `COVERAGE_QUICK_CARD.md`) explaining how to run, interpret, and troubleshoot coverage reports, as well as how to enforce and improve coverage thresholds. These documents provide step-by-step instructions for both Windows and Linux/Mac environments, and clarify what code should and should not be tested. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3480000febd357447dbf814832ab9876b4a10c5a049181dcfdb94def2ca3a2e9R1-R329) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-29d3052154477c94c4470820099eb62154323502f6d5f7abbf7f7fb5e5adea46R1-R78) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c7caa57d888b77c1137643d873343d442bed26f88be2726609b63ba08e0908afR1-R53) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-55dee4e029a21cc997774baf5122dc0c050653ff1fbc8528bce6acf176ea9595R1-R121)
- Included before/after explanations and realistic coverage targets to help the team understand the impact of exclusions and set achievable goals. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fbd04b0cf60f5c013a1db895e84ab002ab8bda5874a4811f53504e3fd370ca02R1-R162) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bbbdc3a245e2ea49b497c1160140b3f87bf28f2c56d160b8fe0bdefcb26e83b7R1-R104) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-55dee4e029a21cc997774baf5122dc0c050653ff1fbc8528bce6acf176ea9595R1-R121)

### 3. CI/CD Integration

- Introduced a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/test-coverage.yml`) that runs tests, enforces an 80% line coverage threshold, generates and uploads HTML reports, and provides clear logs and artifacts for review. The workflow is designed to fail builds if the threshold is not met, ensuring coverage standards are maintained.
- Documentation updated to reflect CI/CD enforcement and provide templates for further automation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3480000febd357447dbf814832ab9876b4a10c5a049181dcfdb94def2ca3a2e9R1-R329) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-29d3052154477c94c4470820099eb62154323502f6d5f7abbf7f7fb5e5adea46R1-R78)

### 4. Coverage Status & Progress Reporting

- Added summary and progress files (`COVERAGE_FIX_SUMMARY.md`, `COVERAGE_QUICK_CARD.md`) that document the team's current coverage status, improvements by controller, and next steps for further increasing coverage. These files serve as a historical record and motivational tool for ongoing quality efforts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bbbdc3a245e2ea49b497c1160140b3f87bf28f2c56d160b8fe0bdefcb26e83b7R1-R104) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-55dee4e029a21cc997774baf5122dc0c050653ff1fbc8528bce6acf176ea9595R1-R121)

---

These changes collectively ensure that coverage metrics are meaningful, actionable, and enforced both locally and in CI, while providing the team with the resources needed to maintain and improve code quality.

body:
Timer increment was applied to wrong player and `lastTick` wasn't reset between moves, causing time jumps and incorrect increment behavior.

## Changes

**Fixed increment application** (`hooks/useGame.ts`)
- Applied increment to `move.color` (player who just moved) instead of `prev.turn` (next player)
- Legacy applies increment before turn switches; Next.js was checking turn after switch

```typescript
// Before: wrong player gets increment
whiteTime: prev.turn === 'w' ? prev.whiteTime + incrementMs : prev.whiteTime

// After: matches legacy
whiteTime: move.color === 'w' ? prev.whiteTime + incrementMs : prev.whiteTime
```

**Fixed timer tick continuity** (`hooks/useGame.ts`)
- Reset `lastTickRef.current` on each move when timer is running
- Prevents time jump artifacts between moves

```typescript
if (!isTimerRunning && game.history().length === 1) {
  startTimer();
} else if (isTimerRunning) {
  lastTickRef.current = Date.now();  // Reset to prevent jump
}
```

**Added parity tests** (`tests/parity/time-controls-parity.test.ts`)
- 23 test cases covering increment timing, tick precision, timeout handling
- Direct legacy vs Next.js comparison tests
- All 337 tests passing

body:
This PR adds the ability to build on the latest macOS runners while still targeting an older version of macOS.

The `CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` is propagated to vcpkg so that all dependencies are also built for the correct version of macOS.

Because OpenSSL was originally fetched via brew installation, its binary would inherently target the version of macOS that it was being installed on. To remedy this, OpenSSL is now fetched from vcpkg.

`windows-macos.yml` is subsequently pruned to no longer spawn unneeded macOS runners.

The deployment target can be queried from a Multipass binary with the command `otool -l multipassd | grep -A 3 LC_BUILD_VERSION`.

Updated licence information in the installer with the appropriate licence as found in the [openssl repository](https://github.com/openssl/openssl). Also, updated the licence information for semver as its source recently changed in #4461.

Verified on a macOS 14 virtual machine. Nested virtualization is only supported on M3 and newer, so you will need to remove the CPU checks in `preinstall-multipassd.sh` and `CPack.distribution.dist.in`.

Closes https://github.com/canonical/multipass/pull/4023
Closes https://github.com/canonical/multipass-private/pull/739

author: wandeman2t-code
body:
# WandeBit (WDB)

A simple fungible token smart contract for the Stacks blockchain, built with Clarinet.

## Overview

WandeBit is a minimal fungible token with 6 decimals and an owner-controlled mint. It supports mint, transfer, burn, metadata (name, symbol, decimals, optional URI), and ownership transfer.

- Name: WandeBit
- Symbol: WDB
- Decimals: 6
- Initial supply: 0 (owner can mint)
- File: `contracts/wandebit.clar`

## Prerequisites

- Clarinet CLI
  - Install via npm: `npm i -g @hirosystems/clarinet`
  - Or see docs: https://docs.hiro.so/clarinet

## Quickstart

```bash
# From repo root
clarinet check
clarinet console
```

Inside the console you can try:
```clarity
;; Mint 100.000000 WDB to the deployer
(contract-call? .wandebit mint tx-sender u100000000)

;; Transfer 1.000000 WDB to another principal
(contract-call? .wandebit transfer 'SP2C2HV0N7ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ u1000000)

;; Check balances
(contract-call? .wandebit get-balance tx-sender)
(contract-call? .wandebit get-balance 'SP2C2HV0N7ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ)
```

## Contract API

Public functions (all return `(response bool uint)` with `ok true` on success; errors use codes below):
- `mint (recipient principal) (amount uint)` — owner only
- `transfer (recipient principal) (amount uint)` — debits `tx-sender`
- `burn (amount uint)` — burns from `tx-sender`
- `set-token-uri (new-uri (optional (string-utf8 256)))` — owner only
- `transfer-ownership (new-owner principal)` — owner only

Read-only functions:
- `get-name () -> (response (string-utf8 32) uint)`
- `get-symbol () -> (response (string-utf8 16) uint)`
- `get-decimals () -> (response uint uint)`
- `get-total-supply () -> (response uint uint)`
- `get-balance (who principal) -> (response uint uint)`
- `get-token-uri () -> (optional (string-utf8 256))`
- `get-contract-owner () -> principal`

Error codes:
- `u100` — not authorized (owner-only)
- `u101` — insufficient balance
- `u102` — invalid amount (must be > u0)
- `u103` — same recipient as sender

## Project structure

- `Clarinet.toml` — project config with `[contracts.wandebit]`
- `contracts/wandebit.clar` — token contract implementation
- `tests/` — place Clarinet tests (optional)

## Common tasks

- Lint/type-check (syntax):
```bash
clarinet check
```

- Local REPL for manual calls:
```bash
clarinet console
```

- Integration environment (miners, stacks-node, etc.):
```bash
clarinet integrate
```

## Security notes

- The owner can mint new tokens and set the token URI. Rotate ownership with `transfer-ownership` when deploying if needed.
- No allowance/approval is implemented; transfers are initiated by the token holder.

## License

MIT

body:
Implements release infrastructure for Soulvan Core 2.0 with automated Unity builds and GitHub Releases integration.

## Changes

- **CI Workflow** (`.github/workflows/build-and-release.yml`)
  - Builds Unity project for Windows x86_64 using game-ci/unity-builder@v4
  - Triggers on `v*.*.*` tags or manual dispatch with custom version
  - Packages as `SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip` and publishes to GitHub Releases
  - Caches Unity Library to optimize build times

- **Documentation** (`README.md`)
  - Rebranded to "Soulvan Core 2.0" with Epic ARPG positioning
  - Added download instructions with direct release links
  - Documented CI workflow setup and triggers
  - Listed modular architecture (contracts, backend, Unity)

- **Version Files**
  - `VERSION`: 2.0.0
  - `CHANGELOG.md`: v2.0.0 entry documenting standardized build flow
  - `backend/package.json`: Version 2.0.0 with hardhat, ethers, express dependencies

## Workflow Example

Tag push triggers automatic build and release:
```bash
git tag v2.0.0
git push origin v2.0.0
# → CI builds Unity project → uploads SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip to Release
```

Manual dispatch for ad-hoc builds:
```yaml
# Actions → Build and Release Soulvan Core → Run workflow
# Input: version = "v2.0.0-rc1"
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement Soulvan Core 2.0 release packaging and documentation, and prepare a tagged build v2.0.0.

Scope
- Add GitHub Actions CI to build the Unity project and publish a downloadable Windows ZIP to GitHub Releases when a tag is pushed (e.g., v2.0.0) or when run manually.
- Update README to reflect the new “Soulvan Core 2.0” naming and download instructions.
- Add VERSION and CHANGELOG entries for v2.0.0.
- Bump backend package version to 2.0.0.

Details and exact file changes
1) Create CI workflow file
- Path: .github/workflows/build-and-release.yml
- Purpose: Build on tag push, zip artifact, upload to Release as SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip
- File contents:

```yaml
name: Build and Release Soulvan Core

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Release version (e.g., v2.0.0). If omitted, uses ref name."
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build-windows:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version != '' && inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Read Unity version from ProjectSettings
        id: unity_version
        run: |
          ver=$(grep 'm_EditorVersion:' unity/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt | sed 's/.*: //')
          echo "version=$ver" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cache Unity Library
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            unity/Library
            unity/Logs
          key: Library-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.unity_version.outputs.version }}
          restore-keys: |
            Library-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Build (Windows x86_64)
        uses: game-ci/unity-builder@v4
        env:
          UNITY_LICENSE: ${{ secrets.UNITY_LICENSE }}
        with:
          projectPath: unity
          unityVersion: ${{ steps.unity_version.outputs.version }}
          targetPlatform: StandaloneWindows64
          buildName: SoulvanCore
          buildsPath: build
          versioning: Custom
          version: ${{ env.VERSION }}

      - name: Package Windows build
        run: |
          cd build
          zip -r SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip StandaloneWindows64 || (echo "Build folder not found" && ls -la && exit 1)
          ls -lh SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip

      - name: Upload artifact (CI preview)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64-${{ env.VERSION }}
          path: build/SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') || inputs.version != ''
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ env.VERSION }}
          name: Soulvan Core ${{ env.VERSION }}
          body: |
            Automated release for Soulvan Core build ${{ env.VERSION }}.
          draft: false
          prerelease: ${{ contains(env.VERSION, 'rc') || contains(env.VERSION, 'beta') || contains(env.VERSION, 'alpha') }}
          files: |
            build/SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip
```

2) Update README with Core naming and download link
- Path: README.md (replace contents or add section at top)
- File contents:

````markdown
# Soulvan Core 2.0

Epic ARPG with kingdom-building and blockchain-linked progression.

## Download

Go to the [Releases](../../releases) page and download:
- `SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip` for the desired version (e.g., `v2.0.0`)

Direct link (replace version if needed):
- https://github.com/44547/soulvan-coin-core/releases/download/v2.0.0/SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip

## Build and Release (CI)

- Workflow: `.github/workflows/build-and-release.yml`
- Triggers:
  - Push a tag like `v2.0.0`
  - Manual dispatch with a `version` input

### One-time setup

1. Add Unity license to repo secrets as `UNITY_LICENSE` (see game-ci activation docs)
2. Ensure the Unity project is in `unity/`
3. Confirm `unity/ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` is correct

### Outputs

- Release asset: `SoulvanCore_Windows_x86_64.zip`

## Modules

body:
Extends the install script to run `unminimize` (for minimal Ubuntu containers) and install `fzf` before configuring dotfiles.

**Changes:**
- Added `sudo unminimize -y` with graceful fallback if command doesn't exist or fails
- Added `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y fzf` with error handling that exits on failure

```bash
# Run unminimize to restore standard packages in minimal Ubuntu containers
echo "Running unminimize..."
if command -v unminimize &> /dev/null; then
    sudo unminimize -y || echo "Warning: unminimize failed. This may be normal if not running in a minimal Ubuntu container."
else
    echo "unminimize command not found, skipping..."
fi

# Update package list and install fzf
echo "Updating package list and installing fzf..."
sudo apt update || { echo "Error: apt update failed"; exit 1; }
sudo apt install -y fzf || { echo "Error: Failed to install fzf"; exit 1; }
```

**Error handling:**
- `unminimize` failures are non-fatal (command may not exist or be applicable)
- `apt` command failures exit immediately to prevent broken state

author: alexanderwiederin
body:
## Fix(state): Fix platform-specific crash in chainman_process_block fuzzer

### Summary
Fixes a crash in the `chainman_process_block` fuzzer that occurred on macOS when paths contained control characters or invalid Unicode. The issue was filesystem-specific: macOS/APFS rejects certain characters that Linux/tmpfs accepts, causing `ChainstateManagerOptions::new()` to fail with unhandled errors.

### Problem
The fuzzer discovered that passing paths with control characters (e.g., `\u{1b}`, `\u{10}`) or invalid Unicode sequences (e.g., `\u{b1c71}`) caused panics on macOS but worked fine on Linux. The code assumed only `CStringCreationFailed` errors were possible, but filesystem validation failures triggered different errors that weren't handled.

**Crash input (base64):** `8rGxsVYbEPf/EACA`

### Solution
1. **Added path sanitization to the library** - `ChainstateManagerOptions::new()` now sanitizes paths before use, filtering to ASCII alphanumeric plus `[_-./]`, rejecting paths >255 chars, and trimming dots
2. **Simplified the fuzzer** - Removed sanitization from the fuzz target and added error handling for `PathValidation` errors

### Changes
- Added `KernelError::PathValidation` variant
- Added `sanitize_path()` helper function in `chainstate.rs`
- Updated fuzzer to handle `PathValidation` as expected error case
- Added tests for path sanitization edge cases

author: antonreinhard
body:
This adds support for runtime generated broadcasting kernels using KernelAbstractions.

Caveats:
- Not compatible with closures by definition, because `@generated` does not allow closures. Could be worked around with `@opaque`, but this feature is still experimental and may be removed, and also would require a lot of rewriting in itself. I'm more inclined to just remove closure support again, I don't think it helped much with compile times anyway. The `@noinline` is doing far better of a job.
- ~~Only one broadcasting kernel can be generated per input type and module. This could maybe be solved, but not easily. The way RGF.jl does it will not work I think, because it relies on non-`isbits` things, which won't work with KA.jl. A simple way to implement would be to return a `Val{UUID}` that identifies the function that has to be passed to the kernel call by the user, but it would be somewhat unintuitive to the user.~~ Fixed by the `KAWrapper` inserting a unique `Val{UUID}` per generated function.
- ~~The generated function can't be overwritten after it has been called once, because we can't force the `@generated` function to recompile, to my knowledge. This is a similar problem to above, with some sort of UUID this wouldn't be a problem.~~ Fixed by `KAWrapper` too.

I added some GPU testing that doesn't run on GPUs for now (because github's GPU runners cost money) but they at least test the KernelAbstractions CPU backend and should make it easier to test locally.

This also removes support for the keyword arguments `closures_size` and `concrete_input_type`. Closures made problems with the kernel abstractions implementation, so they couldn't be used there anyways. A reevaluation of the feature also showed that they don't consistently improve compile times anyway, and the `@inline` is much more significant. The type inference (which `concrete_input_type` was  used for) is therefore now also unnecessary, since that was used to make closures type stable.

If I ever revisit the idea of closures to improve compile times, I will go back to this version and see what I deleted.
